events.title: Banks rescue a large investment fund
events.description: Private banks and securities firms invest in Long-Term Capital Management after heavy losses.

events.title: The euro begins
events.description: Eleven countries adopt a shared currency for financial transactions. Notes and coins come later.

events.title: The September 11 attacks
events.description: Terrorist attacks kill thousands in the United States. Communities mourn and help those affected.

what_happened_next.text:
Bonds led this set over five years. The US share basket finished only a little higher, while the international basket and all three company shares lost value. This was a difficult window for stock investors. It does not prove that stocks always lose or bonds always win; a different starting date can change the result.

The years ahead included a rescue of Long-Term Capital Management after heavy losses, the start of the euro for financial transactions, and the September 11 attacks. Families and communities faced events far more important than market rankings. The chart records investment values through those years, not the full effect of the events on people’s lives.

The bond choice was useful in this particular window because it gained while the featured company shares fell. That does not make bonds risk-free: their prices can also decline. Compare the amount you would have lost in a single company with a mix of assets. The trade-off is about which risks you take, rather than finding one choice that wins forever.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: Thailand changed its currency policy, index funds were drawing money, and companies were changing leaders and products.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The investment mix mattered. Cash and the government-bond choice rose while many shares fell. They did not depend on a particular company succeeding.
reflection.what_faded_away: A well-known brand and a popular theater production did not prevent losses in a company’s shares. Recent market success was not a promise of five more good years.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The coming sequence of crises and market falls was unknown. A sensible plan still had to allow for outcomes that the starting headlines did not predict.
